items.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 1:32PM EST until November 20 at 6:30PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is ongoing.

* WHERE...Northern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Southeastern Orange County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 630 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 131 PM EST, Flooding is ongoing in the warned area. Between 3
and 4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional heavy rainfall is
not expected this aftenroon.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Titusville, Rockledge, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Satellite Beach, Cape
Canaveral, Port Saint John, Titusville Airport, Sharpes, Port
Canaveral, Playalinda Beach, Lone Cabbage Fish Camp, Merritt
Island, Mims, Haulover Canal, Scottsmoor, Patrick Space Force
Base, Indian Harbour Beach and Canaveral Groves.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued November 19 at 11:05PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, northeast winds 25 to 30 knots with
gusts up to 40 knots and seas 11 to 16 feet. For the Small Craft
Advisory, northwest winds 20 to 30 knots with occasional gusts
up to 35 knots and seas 11 to 16 feet expected.

* WHERE...Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 0-20 nm
and Volusia-Brevard County Line to Sebastian Inlet 20-60 nm.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 7 PM EST Friday. For the
Small Craft Advisory, from 7 PM Friday to 7 AM EST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
